title: RepoCoder: Repository-Level Code Completion Through Iterative Retrieval and Generation

key_numbers.metric: Pass Rate, function body (GPT-3.5-Turbo, all repos)

key_numbers.value: K=10 max snippets; window Sw=20/50, Ss=10

budget_tradeoff_detail: Retrieval budget (K=10 snippets, fixed window sizes) held constant across RepoCoder iterations/Oracle; no explicit token-cost-vs-quality sweep reported beyond fixed prompt/generation token caps (4096/2048).
confound_note: In-File vs RepoCoder varies both the presence of retrieval and its content (no cross-file budget at all vs a fixed K=10 retrieval budget); the more controlled contrast (Iter-1/Iter-2 vs Oracle) holds K and window sizes constant while varying only query quality (self-predicted vs ground-truth continuation).

title: CrossCodeEval: A Diverse and Multilingual Benchmark for Cross-File Code Completion

key_numbers.metric: Exact Match, StarCoder-15.5B Python, no-context vs retrieved-context

budget_tradeoff_detail: Retrieved cross-file context capped at 512 BPE tokens per example across BM25/UniXCoder/OpenAI-ada retrievers; adding retrieved context raises StarCoder-15.5B Python EM from 8.82% to 15.72% (oracle: 21.01%).
confound_note: Retriever/representation varied (BM25 lexical vs UniXCoder/ada dense embeddings) at matched top-5 snippets / 512-token budget in the retrieval-method comparison; the separate with-vs-without-context comparison additionally varies budget (0 vs 512 tokens).

title: EVOR: Evolving Retrieval for Code Generation

key_numbers.metric: Execution accuracy (ChatGPT backbone), EVOR vs DocPrompting

budget_tradeoff_detail: Sec. 4.4 reports pass rate as a function of token consumption swept 4k-24k, showing diminishing returns; EVOR's iterative loop consumes ~4x the tokens of DocPrompting for its accuracy gain (Table 7).
confound_note: Primary comparison (EVOR vs Reflexion/DocPrompting, Table 2) varies both knowledge source diversity (docs+web+exec-feedback+code vs single static source) and the iterative query-evolution mechanism jointly, at unmatched token budgets; the repo-level SWE-bench-Lite result is a secondary, less-instrumented experiment.

title: R2C2-Coder: Enhancing and Benchmarking Real-world Repository-level Code Completion Abilities of Code Large Language Models

key_numbers.metric: Ablation EM: without snippet context vs both contexts

budget_tradeoff_detail: Max prompt length fixed at N=4,096 tokens; ablation (Table 5) shows adding abstract-context (AST declarations) and snippet-context (raw code windows) each contribute several points of EM within that fixed budget.
confound_note: Table 5 ablation (with/without abstract context, with/without snippet context) varies representation composition only, holding the N=4,096-token prompt budget and retrieval method (Jaccard) fixed — a budget-matched representation ablation; Table 2/4 main results vary model, fine-tuning, and benchmark simultaneously, not budget-matched.

title: STALL+: Boosting LLM-based Repository-level Code Completion with Static Analysis

key_numbers.metric: Best combined (RAG + static analysis) Java Line EM

budget_tradeoff_detail: in-file context truncated to 2,000 tokens and cross-file context to 3,000 tokens (Sec 4.5); prompting-phase integration adds full hierarchical static-analysis info on top of these truncated baselines, so token counts differ systematically across strategies
confound_note: central comparison varies both the static-analysis integration point (prompting/decoding/post-processing phase) and the resulting prompt content/length simultaneously — budget is not held constant across arms

title: Prometheus: Towards Long-Horizon Codebase Navigation for Repository-Level Problem Solving

key_numbers.metric: Cost reduction / resolution gain from working memory

budget_tradeoff_detail: Working memory reduces inference cost by ~45.4% ($200.79 vs $367.73 across 50 instances) while improving resolution rate by +25.0pp (70% vs 56%) — Section 4.3.1/Figure 7.
confound_note: Ablations remove one agent/memory component at a time (working memory, multiple patch selection, bug reproduction, regression testing) from the full system while holding model and prompts fixed — varies mechanism/pipeline components, not a token-budget-matched representation comparison.

title: SWE-QA: Can Language Models Answer Repository-level Code Questions?

key_numbers.metric: Token cost of agentic frameworks vs direct prompting

budget_tradeoff_detail: Agentic frameworks (SWE-agent/OpenHands) substantially raise QA quality over direct prompting or sliding-window RAG but consume roughly 100x more tokens (Table 8), a steep token-cost-for-accuracy tradeoff with no budget normalization across methods.
confound_note: Comparison across direct prompting, sliding-window RAG, function-chunking RAG, AST-based retrieval, and agentic exploration varies representation/mechanism and token/context budget simultaneously (agentic methods use ~100x more tokens), so accuracy gains cannot be attributed to representation alone.

title: In Line with Context: Repository-Level Code Generation via Context Inlining

key_numbers.metric: RepoExec Exact Match, relative gain over strongest baseline

budget_tradeoff_detail: Backbone LLM context windows (DeepSeek-V3 128K, Qwen3-Coder 262K, GPT-5-mini 400K) are used as-is with no explicit token-budget-vs-quality sweep reported; gains are reported only as relative EM/BLEU improvements over baselines (Sec 4.4, 5.1).
confound_note: Comparison to RAG baselines varies both representation (bidirectional call-graph inlining vs retrieved snippets) and effective prompt content/length, with no matched token budget across methods or across the three differently-sized backbone context windows.

title: Compressing Code Context for LLM-based Issue Resolution

key_numbers.metric: issue resolution rate vs no compression
key_numbers.value: GPT-5.2: 0.578 vs 0.532 (+4.6pp, +8.6% relative); DeepSeek-V3.2 is the +9.2%-relative case

budget_tradeoff_detail: At ~6x compression (51.8-71.3% token reduction), SWEzze improves SWE-bench Verified issue resolution 5.0-9.2% relative over the no-compression baseline; competing baselines target similar ~5-6x ratios but their achieved compression varies widely (LLMLingua-2 ~2.98x, SWE-Pruner 4.10-49.75x), so budgets are not matched exactly across methods (Table 2-3).
confound_note: Central comparison varies the compression mechanism (learned segment-relevance filtering vs generic token-level LLMLingua-2 vs perplexity-ranked LongCodeZip vs reranker-based SWE-Pruner) at roughly similar target ratios, but actual achieved token budgets differ substantially across methods, so ratio and method quality are confounded.

title: Context-as-AI-Service: Surfacing Cross-File Dependency Chains for LLM-Generated Developer Documentation
benchmarks: 2 production SDK case studies (no named public benchmark)

key_numbers.metric: Input tokens, tutorial validation case study
Wall-clock time, tutorial validation case study

budget_tradeoff_detail: CAIS reduces both wall-clock time (22-34%) and input tokens (16-32%) relative to the baseline agent with ordinary repo tools, while surfacing more issues (13 vs 5) - no quality-for-budget tradeoff observed; both cost and quality improved together (Tables 3-4).
confound_note: Baseline vs baseline+CAIS varies both the retrieval mechanism (ordinary file-read/keyword/symbol tools vs a hybrid BM25+dense fused index) and the resulting token budget (CAIS used fewer tokens), so representation and effective budget move together rather than being held constant.

title: Agent4cs: A Multi-agent System for Code Summarization in Large Hierarchical Codebases
venue: EUMAS 2026 (accepted, main track, per arXiv Comments field)

key_numbers.metric: semantic consistency improvement across folder levels (avg)

key_numbers.value: turicreate: 237 files / 1,725 functions (293 files belongs to the pants repository in the same table)

budget_tradeoff_detail: Full child-folder summaries cannot be concatenated into a parent prompt due to context-window limits, so a keyword-extraction agent compresses child summaries into keywords before parent-level summarization; no explicit token counts are given for this budget.
confound_note: Compares the full three-agent bottom-up pipeline (summarization + keyword-extraction + QA agents) against HR-CS/CS-BF baselines; representation (hierarchical tree/AST vs flat), mechanism (multi-agent iterative refinement vs single-pass), and prompt content all vary simultaneously across 7 different backbone LLMs.

title: MM-IssueLoc: A Controlled Benchmark for Evaluating Visual Evidence in Multimodal Repository-Level Issue Localization
confound_note: Evaluated systems (AgentLess, LocAgent, OpenHands agents vs. BM25/dense-embedding retrievers vs. the paper's own MM-IssueLoc-VL-Embedding) differ simultaneously in retriever/agent architecture, tool-use scaffold, and text-only vs. multimodal (+image, +VCE) input condition — not a controlled representation-only or budget-matched comparison.

title: MRCoder: An Efficient Context Selecting Approach for Repository-Level Code Generation

key_numbers.value: up to 52.1% vs RAG; 47.6% vs RepoFormer

budget_tradeoff_detail: MRCoder improves Pass@1 by 52.7% relative (36.5% vs 23.9%, CoderEval K=10) while simultaneously cutting token consumption 30-50% and inference time up to 52.1% versus plain RAG-reporting simultaneous cost and quality gains rather than a tradeoff curve (Table 2, Sec 5.1-5.2).
confound_note: MRCoder vs RAG/RepoFormer baselines varies both the context-selection mechanism (map-reduce draft-guided filtering vs plain top-K similarity retrieval) and the resulting token budget (MRCoder uses fewer tokens), so quality gains are not isolated from the budget reduction-both move together in MRCoder's favor.
